complaint_categories.name: Billing Dispute
complaint_categories.description: Customer disputes an invoice amount, questions a charge, or believes they were billed incorrectly.
escalation_triggers: Customer mentions chargeback or credit card dispute
Disputed amount exceeds EUR 5,000
Customer claims they never signed the contract
Customer uses the word 'fraud' or 'scam'
Second dispute from the same customer in 90 days
required_actions: Acknowledge receipt within SLA
Pull the invoice and contract from CRM
Verify whether the charge matches the agreed Order Form
If billing error confirmed: issue credit note and corrected invoice within 5 business days
If billing is correct: explain the charge with reference to the specific Order Form line item
Document resolution outcome in CRM
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Empathetic and efficient. Customer is stressed about money. Acknowledge the concern first, then explain or resolve. Never sound defensive.

complaint_categories.name: SLA Breach Claim
complaint_categories.description: Customer claims TechForward failed to meet the uptime or response time SLA commitments in the contract.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: SLA breaches may entitle the customer to service credits under contract Section 5.2, and repeated breaches may trigger termination rights.
escalation_triggers: Customer explicitly requests service credits
Customer mentions termination or cancellation as a result of the outage
Claimed downtime exceeds 24 consecutive hours
Customer is an enterprise or public sector account
Incident affects multiple customers simultaneously (systemic incident)
required_actions: Acknowledge within SLA — do not dispute the claim in the first response
Pull the incident log from the infrastructure team to verify uptime data
Calculate any applicable service credits per the contract SLA formula
If credits apply: confirm in writing with a credit note, reference the contract clause
If termination right triggered: escalate immediately to Legal and Account Management
Send a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) summary within 5 business days of resolution
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Professional and accountable. Do not minimize the impact. Acknowledge the disruption, commit to resolution, and provide a timeline. Never make excuses.

complaint_categories.name: Cancellation / Termination Request
complaint_categories.description: Customer requests to cancel their subscription or terminate the contract.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: Termination requests must be classified as: (a) within cooling-off period — full refund required; (b) termination for cause — legal review required; (c) termination for convenience — subject to notice period and fee obligations.
escalation_triggers: Customer invokes a specific contract clause as justification for termination
Customer is terminating due to an alleged TechForward breach
Deal value of the contract exceeds EUR 50,000 per year
Customer is within the statutory cooling-off period (14 days from contract signature for B2C, check contract for B2B)
Customer is a public sector account
required_actions: Classify the termination type: cooling-off, for-cause, or for-convenience
Pull the contract to determine: notice period, refund obligations, and any termination fees
Acknowledge the request in writing — this is important for calculating notice periods
For for-convenience termination: confirm notice period start date and any applicable fees
For for-cause termination: escalate to Legal immediately — do not accept or reject the cause claim
For cooling-off: confirm refund eligibility and initiate refund process with Finance
Offer a save conversation (retention attempt) only if customer has not explicitly invoked a legal right to terminate
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Respectful and calm. Do not pressure or guilt the customer. Understand their reason. If there's a save opportunity, make it naturally. If they have a legal right to leave, honor it professionally — the goal is a clean exit that doesn't become a dispute.

complaint_categories.name: GDPR Data Subject Request (DSR / DSAR)
complaint_categories.description: Customer or individual user exercises a GDPR right: access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), portability (Art. 20), objection (Art. 21), or restriction of processing (Art. 18).
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: GDPR mandates a response within 1 calendar month (extendable by 2 months for complex requests). Failure to respond is a regulatory violation. Maximum fine: EUR 20M or 4% of global annual turnover.
escalation_triggers: Any complaint that explicitly or implicitly invokes GDPR rights
Erasure request ('right to be forgotten') — may conflict with contract data retention obligations
Request from a person who is not the contract signatory (e.g., individual employee of a corporate customer)
Request that appears to be from a lawyer or data protection authority
Request that could affect ongoing legal proceedings
required_actions: IMMEDIATELY log the request date — the 1-month clock starts on the date of receipt
Verify the identity of the requestor before processing (cannot release data to unverified parties)
Classify the request type (access, erasure, portability, etc.)
Route to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) within 4 hours of receipt
Acknowledge receipt to the customer within 24 hours, including expected response timeline
Do NOT attempt to resolve the DSR without DPO involvement
Log in the GDPR DSR register (maintained by Legal/DPO)
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Formal and precise. Acknowledge the request clearly. Use correct GDPR terminology. Do not make any commitments about what data will or will not be deleted until the DPO has assessed the request. Do not be dismissive — these are legal rights.

complaint_categories.name: Suspected Data Breach Notification (Inbound)
complaint_categories.description: Customer reports that they believe there has been a data breach involving their data, or reports suspicious activity in their TechForward account.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: GDPR Art. 33 requires notification to supervisory authority within 72 hours of TechForward becoming aware of a breach. If customer notifies us, the clock starts. Internal incident response must activate immediately.
escalation_triggers: Any mention of unauthorized access to data
Any mention of data appearing in unexpected places
Any mention of suspicious logins, emails, or activity
Customer reports that their customer data (not just their TechForward account data) may have been exposed
required_actions: IMMEDIATELY escalate to the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) — do not investigate independently
Do NOT confirm or deny whether a breach has occurred — this must come from the SIRT
Acknowledge receipt to the customer within 1 hour: 'We take this very seriously and our security team is investigating'
Log the report with exact timestamp, customer ID, and description
Do NOT discuss the incident details with anyone outside the SIRT and Legal
SIRT will notify the DPO; DPO will assess GDPR notification obligation (72-hour clock to supervisory authority)
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Calm, serious, and immediate. The customer is alarmed. Acknowledge their report seriously without speculating. Do not downplay the concern. Do not say 'it's probably nothing.' Give them a clear next step and timeline.

complaint_categories.name: Onboarding / Delivery Failure
complaint_categories.description: Customer reports that implementation, configuration, or professional services deliverables were not delivered on time, incompletely, or not to the agreed specification.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: Delivery failures may constitute a contract breach, triggering the 30-day cure period under the contract. If not remedied, customer may have termination rights.
escalation_triggers: Customer explicitly invokes contract breach or threatens termination
Delay exceeds 30 days beyond agreed milestone date
Customer has already given a cure notice (any previous written complaint about the same issue)
Professional services value exceeds EUR 20,000
Failure is causing the customer measurable business harm (financial loss, regulatory penalty)
required_actions: Acknowledge within SLA — validate the customer's experience
Pull the SOW and project timeline from the project management system
Identify whether the delay is on TechForward's side or due to customer dependencies
Engage the project delivery team within 24 hours to get a revised timeline
If TechForward at fault: issue a formal cure plan with specific dates and commitments
If customer dependencies are the cause: document clearly in writing (this is important for liability purposes)
Escalate to Legal if the customer has given written notice of breach (cure period has started)
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Accountable and proactive. Do not deflect blame immediately — even if the customer is partly responsible. Acknowledge the frustration. Commit to concrete next steps with dates. Follow up before the customer has to ask again.

complaint_categories.name: Product Bug / Feature Complaint
complaint_categories.description: Customer reports a software bug, unexpected behavior, missing feature, or deterioration in platform performance.
escalation_triggers: Bug causes complete inability to use core platform features (Priority 1)
Bug causes data loss or data corruption
Bug affects regulatory compliance features (audit trail, export, data deletion)
Customer has raised the same bug 3 or more times without resolution
Customer is an enterprise or premium SLA account (different response SLA applies)
required_actions: Acknowledge the report and assign a ticket number
Reproduce or verify the bug with the technical support team
Classify bug severity: P1 (critical/data loss), P2 (core feature broken), P3 (inconvenient), P4 (cosmetic)
P1 bugs: escalate to engineering on-call immediately; update customer every 2 hours
P2 bugs: engineering team response within 1 business day; fix timeline within 5 days
P3/P4 bugs: add to backlog; keep customer informed of target release
Send a resolution confirmation when fixed and deployed
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Technically empathetic. The customer is frustrated that something doesn't work. Validate the frustration, provide a clear ticket reference so they feel heard, and give realistic timelines. Avoid 'this is working as designed' as a dismissal — understand their workflow first.

complaint_categories.name: Refund Request
complaint_categories.description: Customer requests a full or partial refund of fees paid.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: Refund eligibility depends on contract type, termination clause, and whether there was a service failure. Standard subscription contracts are non-refundable for convenience termination. Refunds triggered by TechForward's breach require Legal review.
escalation_triggers: Refund requested is above EUR 1,000
Refund is claimed due to TechForward's breach (not customer's choice to cancel)
Customer is within statutory cooling-off period
Customer has initiated a credit card chargeback
Refund request accompanies a threat of legal action
required_actions: Pull the contract to determine the applicable refund policy (Section 4.4)
Classify the refund basis: cooling-off, service failure, or convenience
Cooling-off (within 14 days of signature, B2C or where contractually agreed): process full refund
Service failure refunds: escalate to Legal to assess contract breach and refund obligation
Convenience termination: prepaid fees are non-refundable per standard contract — explain clearly and without apology
Document the decision with the contract clause reference in CRM
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Empathetic but clear. If the contract says no refund, explain why plainly — don't invent excuses. If a refund is due, confirm it quickly and give a payment timeline. Customers who are told 'no' clearly and respectfully accept it better than customers who feel stalled.

complaint_categories.name: Account Access / Locked Out
complaint_categories.description: Customer cannot access their TechForward account — locked out, credentials lost, MFA issues, or access revoked incorrectly.
escalation_triggers: Account was disabled by TechForward (not user error) — check if related to payment dispute
Customer claims access was revoked without notice
Access issue is affecting a live production system (enterprise customer)
Suspicious login activity reported alongside access issue (treat as potential breach — see CAT-05)
required_actions: Verify customer identity before taking any action on the account
Check account status in the admin console: active / suspended / disabled
If suspended due to non-payment: confirm with Finance before restoring access
If technical lockout: technical support to resolve within SLA
Document the action taken and reason in the audit log
Follow up to confirm access is restored
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Fast and practical. The customer is blocked from doing their job. Acknowledge immediately, give them a reference number, and resolve as quickly as possible. If it takes more than 1 hour, provide an interim update.

complaint_categories.name: Legal Threat / Formal Notice
complaint_categories.description: Customer sends a formal complaint, pre-litigation letter, lawyer correspondence, or explicitly threatens legal action.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: Any formal legal notice or pre-litigation communication must be handled by Legal. Anything the agent says can be used in subsequent proceedings. No substantive response should be sent without Legal approval.
escalation_triggers: Email mentions 'legal action', 'litigation', 'court', 'solicitor', 'Rechtsanwalt', 'claim', 'damages', or 'lawsuit'
Email is sent from a law firm or legal representative
Email references a specific statutory right or contract clause as the basis for a claim
Customer says they have already filed a complaint with a regulatory authority (Datenschutzbehörde, BaFin, etc.)
Email requests that all communication be directed to their legal representative
required_actions: Do NOT send any substantive response without Legal sign-off
Acknowledge receipt only: 'Thank you for your message. We are reviewing it and will respond shortly.'
Forward immediately to the Legal team lead and the relevant Account Manager
Log the date and time of receipt — this may be the start of a legal deadline
Preserve all related correspondence and do not delete any records
Legal team will take over the response within 2 business days
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Neutral and non-committal. The acknowledgment should be polite but contain no admissions, no apologies, and no statements about what TechForward will or will not do. Just: 'We have received your message and are reviewing it.'

complaint_categories.name: Complaint About a TechForward Employee
complaint_categories.description: Customer complains about the conduct, behavior, or communication of a TechForward employee or contractor.
complaint_categories.legal_significance_reason: Employee conduct complaints may have HR, employment law, and liability implications. They must not be investigated or dismissed by the customer care agent.
escalation_triggers: Any complaint about employee behavior
Allegation of harassment, discrimination, or misconduct
Complaint about communication from a named individual
required_actions: Acknowledge the complaint with sincerity — do not minimize or dismiss
Do NOT name, identify, or defend the employee in question
Do NOT investigate or promise an outcome
Route to the Customer Care Manager and HR within 4 hours
Confirm to the customer that the complaint has been registered and will be reviewed by the appropriate team
Ensure no further contact from the named employee with that customer pending investigation
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Empathetic and non-defensive. The customer felt uncomfortable or mistreated. Validate their experience without making factual claims about what happened. 'We take feedback about our team very seriously' is the right tone.

complaint_categories.name: General Dissatisfaction / Vague Complaint
complaint_categories.description: Customer expresses frustration, dissatisfaction, or disappointment without a specific actionable complaint — or a complaint that doesn't fit another category.
escalation_triggers: Complaint becomes specific and fits another category on closer reading — re-classify
Customer has submitted the same vague complaint more than twice
Customer is a high-value account (enterprise tier)
required_actions: Read carefully for any hidden specific complaint — re-classify if found
Ask one clarifying question to understand what resolution the customer is looking for
Offer to connect the customer with their Account Manager for a review call
Document the complaint and any feedback themes in CRM for product/service improvement tracking
complaint_categories.tone_guidance: Curious and warm. The customer is unhappy but doesn't know how to articulate it. Ask open questions, show you care, and try to find the real issue. Don't close the ticket without understanding what they actually wanted.
